metadata.title: Confidently Wrong.
metadata.note: Weekly update. Narrator Muskan, @HumanitariansAI, banner 'Vendor Intelligence'. ONE insight: every bug this week was an assumption nobody verified — that the model had the evidence, that the fix reached old data, that a no-error system was working. Rule: don't assume, verify. Bookends render (composer/verdict/handoff/outro); body B01-B04 are house-style 4K PIL cards in media/. DOUBLE-CHECK LAW: every detail from the creator's own change log (Ajay K. Puri, AMD equity-plan amendment, boilerplate title, 400→900 chars, 8 rows / 955 total, Langfuse silent trace + flush crash).

skin_warnings: B00: palette=claude but the cold open is 'ClaudeComposerAsk916' — COLD OPEN LAW wants ClaudeComposerAsk
END: palette=claude but the outro is 'un-annotated' — OUTRO LAW wants ClaudeTitleOutro

metadata.reformat: center-cut, focus-aware; pantry/<bid>-916.* is the human replacement slot; -916 overrides honored

beats.narration_text: Hey, I'm Muskan. This week my vendor tracker was confidently wrong, five different ways. Empty summaries, an invented executive departure, tracing that logged nothing. Every one came down to the same thing: an assumption nobody checked.

props.command: Audit the SEC pipeline and the tracing — is what we store actually true, and is what looks like it's working really working?

beats.narration_text: First, the summaries were empty. The AI wrote from the headline alone, while the real filing text sat unused in the database. I passed the filing in. A generic, an officer change may indicate a shift, became the departure of Ajay K. Puri, head of worldwide field operations.

show.event: the generic BEFORE box appears, greyed

props.caption: feed the model the filing, not the headline

beats.narration_text: Worse, it invented a departure that never happened. Every filing of this type opens with the same boilerplate, departure of directors or certain officers. The AI saw the word departure and reported one, for an AMD filing that was really an equity-plan amendment. I stripped the boilerplate. AMD reads correctly now.

props.caption: strip the boilerplate, or the model repeats it as fact

beats.narration_text: Then, fixing the code didn't fix the data. The collector skips anything it's seen, matched on the headline, so the bad rows stayed. I wrote a backfill to rewrite them in place, dry-run by default, saving every original. Eight rows corrected, nothing deleted.

props.caption: a code fix leaves the old rows lying

beats.narration_text: And tracing looked fine, but logged nothing. A broad catch-all had been swallowing the error, silently. Fixing it uncovered a second bug that would have crashed brief generation outright. I shipped both, and verified by fetching the trace back from the server.

props.caption: a silent success is not a success

beats.narration_text: Five bugs, one lesson. Every one was an assumption nobody checked. That the model had the evidence. That the fix reached the old data. That a system printing no errors was working. Don't assume. Verify.

artifactLines: Assumed the model had the filing — it summarized the headline, so summaries were empty.
Assumed a boilerplate title was fact — it invented an officer departure that never happened.
Assumed the fix reached old rows — the collector skipped them; a backfill fixed 8, originals saved.
Assumed tracing worked — it was silently off, hiding a second crash. Verified by fetching the trace back.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Take one number or summary your AI gave you, and ask: what real evidence is this based on, and have I checked it against the source? If you can't point to the evidence, don't ship it. It's the cheapest bug insurance there is.

props.command: Take one number or summary my AI produced. What real evidence is it based on? Show me the source text, and flag anything the output claims that the source doesn't support.

beats.narration_text: Confidently wrong. More fixes next week. Humanitarians AI.
